messages:
tara: Heads-up 1FYI
I noticed a few issues in the SDK snippets for streaming+pagination across py/ts/go. Can we coordinate quick PRs? The doc page has mixed terminology (cursor vs resume_token) and the retry example is missing jitter.

alex: I can patch Python today. I want to keep the streaming example minimal but show how to cancel and how to resume with tokens. Will add a short Troubleshooting blurb.

ben: I'll take TS. I'll include both callback and async-iterator patterns and a small note about connection leakage. Will link to the new pagination spec at https://github.com/redwood-inference/specs/pagination.

nina: I'll do Go and add an example using the manual backoff loop. Also will add a short test snippet that CI can run to catch flaky retry behavior.

kevin: Two quick asks: 1) Add exponential backoff with small random jitter (see snippet below) 2) Add stream cancellation in TS using AbortController example.

kevin: ```python
# jittered exponential backoff sample
import random, time
for attempt in range(5):
    try:
        out = client.responses.stream(...)
        break
    except TransientError:
        sleep = 0.1 * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 0.05)
        time.sleep(sleep)
```

alex: I'll copy Kevin's pattern into the Python PR and include a short note: "Prefer small jitter to avoid thundering herd in tests." Also adding cache/prefix note for KV cache so users don't get OOMs with long prefixes.

ben: For TS I'll show both: Promise/then-based callback and for-await-of iterator. I'll also show how to abort: ```ts
const controller = new AbortController();
fetchStream({signal: controller.signal});
// later
controller.abort();
```

nina: Go snippet will show context cancellation and the retry loop using time.Sleep + jitter. Example: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
// cancel() when done
for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
    resp, err := client.Stream(ctx, req)
    if err == nil { break }
    time.Sleep(time.Duration(100*(1<<i))*time.Millisecond + time.Duration(rand.Intn(50))*time.Millisecond)
}
```

tara: Thanks. A couple process notes: please open separate tiny PRs per language and one cross-lang migration PR that links them. Label language PRs with docs-easy. The migration PR should contain a single one-page sandbox showing side-by-side py/ts/go snippets. That made the previous rollouts much easier.

ben: Makes sense. I'll open #4922 for TS and tag @tara. Nina, you can open #4923 for Go. Alex, you mentioned you already started Python?

alex: Yes, Python PR #4921 is up (small rewrite + troubleshooting). CI showed one link failure (old internal pagination doc). I replaced it with the new spec URL. docs-bot shows linter warnings for line length in a code block, I'll fix.

docs-bot: (docs-bot) CI for #4921: link-check failed -> updated external link required. Lint: one line-length warning.

ben: Opened TS PR #4922 and added the AbortController and async iterator examples. Also added a short compatibility note: "v0.9 uses cursor param; v1.0+ uses resume_token."

nina: Opening Go PR #4923 now. Will add a short test in test/snippets/retry_jitter_test.go to exercise the backoff loop so we don't regress.

kevin: For the migration PR please include a small compatibility table for SDK versions (v0.9, v1.0) and a short paragraph about what to change when upgrading (param rename, small API ergonomics). Also mention that streaming behavior may change if users added custom batching.

tara: One editorial nit: in the migration note, avoid deep implementation details about KV cache internals. High-level advice only. Link to infra doc if someone needs deep-dive.

alex: Good point. I'll keep migration note high-level and link to infra doc if needed. Planning PR numbers: #4921 (py, already open), #4922 (ts), #4923 (go), #4924 (migration note + sandbox).

ben: Will add @tara as reviewer on #4922. Tagging docs-easy. Please also add `docs-urgent` label to the migration note if we want fast visibility.

nina: PR #4923 posted. cc @kevin for jitter snippet review. I'll include the test and a short README for the snippet folder.

kevin: Reviewing #4923 now. Quick suggestion: tighten the jitter range in the Go example to avoid >500ms sleeps during unit tests. Use rand.Intn(50) ms.

alex: I fixed the line length and the external link in #4921. CI passing now. Merging this first so Python docs are updated.

docs-bot: (docs-bot) #4921 merged. Link check OK.

ben: Merged #4922 after addressing a wording nit. CI green. #4924 (migration) will reference both merged PRs and Nina's PR when merged.

nina: #4923 merged after Kevin's nit. Added the test and short README.

tara: Excellent. Can someone paste the migration PR link here once you open it? I'll give it a quick editorial pass and then we can ship.

ben: Opening #4924 now (migration & sandbox). Pasting link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4924

alex: Reviewing #4924 for troubleshooting phrasing. Added a short section "Timeouts vs Retries" with example parameter values.

kevin: LGTM from my side. Small suggestion to add a cross-ref to the SDK changelog for v1.0 release notes.

ben: Added the changelog link. Labelled migration PR `docs-urgent` for visibility.

tara: Thanks everyone. This was tidy. Closing the loop here . If anything else pops up, start a new thread. :tada:
